summary: Goal: take the asl-core v3 prototype to the architecture-v5 design (lens-core crate, strict reader, Claude/Codex parsers, status table, Change Detector with fake Clock, Project Resolver, redaction, settings.json, lens-wsl-helper, NDJSON receiver, helper supervisor, IPC, Tauri wiring, UI). 34 tasks. EXECUTION ORDER (unique, ascending id): T001 rename > T002 finish-rename > T003 consts > T004 change-detector > T005 reader > T006 schema > T007 resolver > T008 helper-cli > T009 clock-offset > T010 redact > T011 process > T012 claude > T013 codex > T014 reader-2 > T015 ndjson > T016 settings > T017 distro > T018 claude-2 > T019 codex-2 > T020 ndjson-2 > T021 status-table > T022 initial-scan > T023 aggregator > T024 helper-serve > T025 read-only(F22) > T026 aggregator-2 > T027 sup1 > T028 ipc-1 > T029 sup2 > T030 sup3 > T031 ipc-2 > T032 tauri > T033 ui > T034 audit. ORDERING RULE: layer (1 + max layer of dependencies) ascending, then risk high > medium > low, then title in ASCII order; ids follow exactly this order, so every dependency has a smaller id. RISK PLACEMENT: the minimal prerequisite chain is T001 rename, T002 finish-rename (7 files name the old crate, over the 5-change limit, hence two tasks) and T003 consts; all three are low risk and 1 round. The riskiest spikes follow immediately and depend only on what they use: change detector T004 (file watching; needs consts) and reader T005 (parsing I/O; needs consts) are the first layer after the chain (layer 4); process wrapper T011 comes right after the detector because its F9 watchdog needs FakeClock from clock.rs; Claude T012 and Codex T013 parsers depend on reader part 1 only; WSL distro polling T017 is rated high (Lxss registry and wsl.exe output are Windows-only and untestable in CI) and depends only on schema and process (the disabled list is a parameter), so it sits at layer 6, the earliest layer its dependencies allow (right after the process wrapper), ahead of the supervisor that consumes it. Big tasks were split so none exceeds 6 acceptance lines or 2 estimated rounds: reader, Claude, Codex, NDJSON, aggregator and IPC each have a part 1/2 and 2/2; other long lists were merged. SAFE STOP POINTS: every task ends with cargo test --workspace green (npm run build is verified where the frontend changes and unchanged elsewhere), so stopping after any task leaves a building, passing repository. Each task's stop state names what is usable, an rg check proving what is not usable yet (exit 1 while the downstream tests/wiring are absent; valid at that task's own stop point only), and how to revert. REVERT: git revert of a task's commit, after reverting its dependents (later ids first); no task changes a data format. Persisted state: only %APPDATA%\agent-session-lens\settings.json (plus .bad) is ever written, and only by the app at run time via the settings/IPC path; T016 (store, temp dir in tests), T031 (first writer), T030 (reader only) and T032 (app start-up) touch it; reverting them never touches the file, delete it by hand to reset. Not usable at stop (but still green): after T032 (Tauri wiring) the backend is live but the old UI is empty because the get_snapshot shim returns null, so the app is user-usable only after T033. T032 keeps a get_snapshot shim (src/App.tsx still invokes it); T033 removes the shim and its caller together. VERIFY COMMANDS are POSIX shell (Git Bash on the Windows host), run from the repository root; commands that can run on the current v3 tree were pre-run and their observed exit codes are listed in the assumptions. Windows-only parts (Job Object, Lxss registry, wsl.exe) are cfg(windows) with portable fakes and run on this Windows host. Out of scope per the design: CI, packaging, helper distribution, operations.

tasks.title: Injectable Clock and Change Detector
tasks.intent: Add clock.rs (Clock trait with real and fake implementations) and change_detector.rs: notify events are collapsed per DEBOUNCE_MS (200); files with mtime within HOT_WINDOW_SECS (900) get a (size, mtime) check every HOT_POLL_SECS (2); the root is reconciled every RECONCILE_SECS (60); notify overflow (IN_Q_OVERFLOW, max_user_watches exceeded, ReadDirectoryChangesW overflow) triggers an immediate reconcile; failures use `pub fn backoff_secs(n) = min(2^(n-1), BACKOFF_MAX_SECS)` (n reset to 1 on success), which the supervisor later reuses. Tests drive only the fake Clock with notify disabled; no wall-clock sleeps. Risk (high): file-change notification is the flagged fragile area; real overflow of inotify/ReadDirectoryChangesW cannot be provoked in a unit test, so overflow is injected as an event and only the reaction is tested, the backend mapping (which notify error/flag means overflow) stays unverified.
